options: Software that only runs on one office server
The delivery of pay-as-you-go computing services hosted on infrastructure over the internet
A backup of your files on a USB drive
A programming language for servers
questions.explain: Cloud services (storage, databases, networking, analytics…) are rented over the internet and paid for as you use them.
questions.evidence: The Cloud, or Cloud Computing, is the delivery of a wide range of pay-as-you-go computing services hosted on an infrastructure over the internet.

questions.q: A private cloud refers to computing resources that are…
options: used exclusively by a single business or organization
shared by many companies over the public internet
provided free of charge by governments
stored only on personal laptops
questions.explain: A private cloud is dedicated to one organisation and runs on a private network.
questions.evidence: Private cloud: refers to cloud computing resources used exclusively by a single business or organization

options: A bug that only appears in production
A licence that forbids reuse
A relationship where one software component relies on another to work properly
A container that has stopped running
questions.explain: Conflicting or missing dependencies are a classic installation problem that containers help solve.
questions.evidence: A software dependency is a relationship between software components where one component relies on the other to work properly.

options: A running instance of an application
A screenshot of a server's desktop
An account on a container registry
The template from which particular containers are created
questions.explain: Images are templates; containers are running (or stopped) instances created from them.
questions.evidence: a container image is the template from which particular instances of containers will be created

options: An online repository of container images
A command that deletes old containers
A configuration file format
A monitoring dashboard
questions.explain: Registries such as Docker Hub and quay.io host images you can pull and reuse.
questions.evidence: The Docker Hub is an online repository of container images, a vast number of which are publicly available.

options: A log of every container you have run
A plain text file with keywords and commands used to create a new container image
A compressed copy of a container
A list of registry passwords
questions.explain: Writing the build steps in a Dockerfile makes images reproducible, unlike snapshotting an interactive session.
questions.evidence: A Dockerfile is a plain text file with keywords and commands that can be used to create a new container image.

options: Locking files so only one person can edit them
Numbering releases with dates
Keeping track of changes to your code over time
Checking which software versions users have installed
questions.explain: Version control records every change, with clear commit messages explaining why.
questions.evidence: Version control means keeping track of changes to your code over time.

questions.q: Why run automated tests every time you make a change?
options: It removes the need for user research
You find defects more quickly
It makes deployments slower but safer
Tests are required by law
questions.explain: Fast feedback from continuous integration means problems are caught and fixed early.
questions.evidence: By testing your code automatically every time you make a change, you’ll be able to find defects more quickly.

options: Monitoring memory use inside your servers
Asking users to report outages
Reviewing logs once a month
Monitoring set up outside your service that keeps checking it even if your infrastructure goes down
questions.explain: Internal monitoring watches metrics inside your infrastructure; external monitoring still works when that infrastructure fails.
questions.evidence: External monitoring is the monitoring you should set up outside of your service which keeps checking your systems even if your infrastructure goes down.

questions.q: To maximise uptime, how many states should your service be designed to have?
options: More possible states than simply ‘on’ or ‘off’
Exactly two: on and off
Only ‘on’ — downtime is never acceptable
It doesn't matter as long as you have backups
questions.explain: Graceful degradation (for example read-only modes) keeps a service useful when parts of it fail.
questions.evidence: Your service should have more possible states than simply ‘on’ or ‘off’.
